title: String Transformation
statement:
You get two strings `s` and `t` of the same length `n`, and an integer `k`. One operation chooses a length `l` with `0 < l < n` and replaces `s` by its last `l` characters followed by its first `n - l` characters (the suffix of length `l` is moved to the front).

Count the sequences of exactly `k` operations that turn `s` into `t`. Two sequences are different when some step chooses a different `l`, even if the strings they produce look the same. Return the count modulo `10^9 + 7` (it is `0` when `t` cannot be reached).
constraints: s and t contain only lowercase English letters
signature: int numberOfWays(String s, String t, long k)
notes:
## Intuition

Every operation is a rotation, so after any number of steps `s` is always some rotation of itself, described by an offset in `0..n-1`. One step adds a nonzero amount to the offset, and all `n - 1` nonzero amounts are allowed. So the problem splits in two:

- **Which offsets spell `t`?** Search for `t` inside `s + s` with KMP; each match start is an offset that works.
- **How many `k`-step sequences land on a given offset?** By symmetry every nonzero offset is reached equally often, so only two numbers matter: ways to end at offset 0, and ways to end at one particular nonzero offset.

Simulating all `k` steps is hopeless for `k` up to `10^15`, so the two-state recurrence is raised to the `k`-th power by repeated squaring.

## Approach

1. Build the KMP failure table `fail` of `t`.
2. Scan `text = s + s` without its last character, so each start `0..n-1` is seen once. A match ending at `i = n - 1` means `s` already equals `t` (`sameAsStart`); every other match counts toward `otherMatches`.
3. From offset 0 a step always leaves it (`n - 1` ways to any nonzero offset); from a nonzero offset there is 1 way back to 0 and `n - 2` ways to another nonzero offset. That is the matrix `step = [[0, n-1], [1, n-2]]`.
4. Raise `step` to the power `k` in `result`. Its first column gives `atStart` and `atOther`, the ways to end at 0 and at one fixed nonzero offset.
5. Return `sameAsStart * atStart + otherMatches * atOther` modulo `10^9 + 7`.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "abcd"`, `t = "cdab"`, `k = 2`. `text = "abcdabc"` and the only match starts at index 2, so `sameAsStart = 0` and `otherMatches = 1`. With `n = 4`, `step = [[0, 3], [1, 2]]`, and its square is `[[3, 6], [2, 7]]`. So `atStart = 3` and `atOther = 2`, and the answer is `0 * 3 + 1 * 2 = 2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n + log k): KMP is linear and the 2-by-2 power takes O(log k) multiplications.
- Space: O(n) for the failure table and the doubled text.

## Pitfalls

- Count matches only at starts `0..n-1`; scanning the full `s + s` would count offset 0 twice.
- Offset 0 needs its own count: with `k = 1` you can never stay put, even if `s` equals `t`.
- Products of two residues exceed 2^53, so use `BigInt` (or a 64-bit type) before taking the modulus.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `fail` | KMP failure table of `t` |
| `len` | length of the current partial match |
| `sameAsStart` | 1 if `s` already equals `t` |
| `otherMatches` | number of nonzero offsets whose rotation equals `t` |
| `step`, `result` | the one-step matrix and its running power |
| `power` | the part of `k` still to apply |
| `atStart`, `atOther` | ways to end at offset 0 and at one fixed nonzero offset |

narration.4: The failure table: fail[i] is the longest proper prefix of t that is also a suffix of t[0..i].
narration.7: Fall back through shorter borders until the next character of t can extend the match.
narration.11: Doubling s (minus one character) lists every rotation of s exactly once as a window.
narration.15: Walk the text, extending or shrinking the current match with the failure table.
narration.18: A whole copy of t ends here, so the rotation starting at i - n + 1 equals t.
narration.19: A match ending at n - 1 starts at 0: s already equals t.
narration.20: Any other start is a nonzero rotation that spells t.
narration.30: The identity matrix: zero steps taken so far.
narration.31: One step: from offset 0 there are n - 1 ways out; from a nonzero offset 1 way back and n - 2 ways elsewhere.
narration.33: Repeated squaring applies k steps in O(log k) matrix products.
narration.34: When the low bit of the remaining power is set, fold the current square into the result.
narration.38: First column, top: the ways to end back at offset 0 after k steps.
narration.39: First column, bottom: the ways to end at one particular nonzero offset.
narration.40: Each matching offset contributes its own count; add them up modulo 10^9 + 7.
